ELEVEN FUNDS IS A SMALL CROSS-SECTION, nine before XLRE/XLC exist. laggard_count 4 of 11 means one fund entering or leaving the bottom quartile is a large fraction of the signal — §48's finding (twenty positions were three to six independent bets) applies with less room.

SECTOR CHEAPNESS PERSISTS FOR CORRECT REASONS. Period c contains 2014-2019 energy: six years at 12%+ drawdown with a base that stabilized and failed repeatedly. The time stop bounds each loss at ~9 weeks; it does not bound how many times the same sector re-arms.

THE MANDATES WERE REMAPPED in the early 2000s (XLV was Consumer Services before Health Care) — the funds are continuous, but 2000-2006 rotation rotates between slightly different things than today's tickers name.

judge_model IS A DISTRIBUTION STAND-IN with no prompt (divergence #14/ #15) — and Phase 14 just changed the LIVE judge's context materially, so the gap between judge_model and the shipped judge is at its widest ever.

A PASS WOULD NOT BE AN EDGE. It would say one candidate cleared one bar on one universe, on a simulator with open divergences against live. §57 froze the licence, and the reading rule above spends none of it.

READING RULE across s66a-d, committed before any run: (1) THIS CANDIDATE CAN NEVER LICENSE AN EDGE REGISTRATION, REGARDLESS OF OUTCOME — its own literature predicts the total-return bar fails, and a surprise 3-of-4 pass on a handful of monthly switches is exactly the luck this record warns about; (2) candidate max_drawdown_pct at least 5pp shallower than SPY's benchmark drawdown in 3 or more periods AND clause (b) passing in 2 or more resolves 'note as a possible ensemble risk-overlay', a future separately-registered question; (3) anything else closes the candidate.
